notes.title: New DLC — Coming Soon!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/5628ed82c9839dd5fb5afc8200321afd4cbccf24.jpg[/img]
[h1]Ahoy![/h1]
[b]September 26[/b] marks the start of the open beta for version 1.6. The changelog is so massive that I’ll begin writing it down this Monday.

So today — let’s keep it short and to the point.

[h2]Supporter Pack[/h2]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2749310/Caribbean_Legend__Supporter_Pack/

For a year and a half, the Supporter Pack remained exclusive to those who purchased the most expensive pre-orders, contest winners, and our friends. That’s more than two hundred people without whom our beloved game would never have seen the light of day.

Now we’ve added two achievements, a mini-quest, and five new items to the pack. They truly shine in version 1.6, as you can build 1–2 strong and unique builds around them.

[b]How much does it cost?[/b]
$9.99

[b]Do I need to repurchase the new items if I already own this DLC?[/b]
No, everything will be added automatically. Starting the new game is not required.

[b]Will the DLC work with the 1.6 beta?[/b]
Yes — and with version 1.5.1 as well.

[h2]Fleeing on the Global Map[/h2]
It’s finally here! In the past, if an enemy caught you, you had no choice but to fight, run away in naval mode, reload, or use exploits. There were simply no stats or mechanics that gave you control over your movement on the global map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/7a499049042e8f3a9f4adf8736866a86595031c9.gif[/img]

With version 1.6, you’ll be able to temporarily neutralize any pursuer. Your chances depend on your equipment, perks, and build, as well as the composition, size, cargo, and condition of your fleet. And of course — a bit of luck, because what’s a pirate’s life without it?

What we do — we do for you.
ːjollyrː

notes.title: GD Notes #4. Perks and Items. Q&A.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/1ce45b7b8cb16f0e0b13513d7bf0ed6d0eb34b80.jpg[/img]
[h1]Ahoy![/h1]

Hoist the topsail and set a course for the Bay of Creativity!  
Kirill here — great to see you again.  

It’s been a while since our last chat, so these GD Notes are going to be a long, packed with fresh details.  

Back in Dev Diary VII we teased not one but two new gameplay systems, both tightly linked to each other. The response was huge, and the community had plenty of questions. Time to dive in and clear things up.  
[hr][/hr]  
[h2]Descriptors[/h2]  
Descriptors are special item traits. They can carry unique mechanics and interact with perks in powerful ways.  

Take the [b]Schiavona[/b] for example:  
[list]  
[*]Class: Coldarm  
[*]Stats: damage and weight  
[*]Descriptors: Heavy, Long, Straight, Fancy  
[/list]  
Damage and weight are self-explanatory. Descriptors, however, open up a much deeper layer of gameplay.  
[hr][/hr]  
[h3]Bonuses[/h3]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/e6c74d99dc03881bee5a9364f41c2e05730d2005.png[/img]
Some Descriptors work on their own and stack passive bonuses.  

For instance, Fancy and Plain items (opposites of each other) boost Charisma or Stealth for every equipped slot.  
Want more recruits at the tavern? Go all in on Fancy gear.  
Dream of becoming a terror of the seas — build an Exotic set.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/94250fe2956f05f2f3908b8667cc5280e87bfe58.png[/img]
Need to sneak past patrols or make a quick getaway? Equip a full set of Plain items.  
[hr][/hr]  
[h3]Synergy[/h3]  
Nearly every Descriptor now ties directly into personal perks.  
In the Adventurer tree, for example, you’ll find the perk [b]Tailored Fit[/b].  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/769b08f1d09aac211afa4cec6cc1f86380896d65.png[/img]
It strengthens the synergy between Plain and Fancy items.  

But the flashiest examples are perks based on weapon Descriptors:  
[list]  
[*][b]Heavy Hand[/b] — +15% damage with Heavy weapons, unlocks the advanced Heavy Attack.  
[*][b]Palace Guard[/b] — Heavy Curved weapons: +15% damage with any attack and +5% with Group Attacks.  
[*][b]Cunning Strike[/b] — Light weapons: +3% crit chance and +10% backstab damage.  
[*][b]Exhaustion[/b] — Parrying with Short weapons drains +20% more enemy stamina.  
[*][b]Perfect Balance[/b] — Medium weapons reduce incoming damage by 10%.  
[*][b]Kern[/b] — Multi-Shot firearms: +8% damage and +4% reload speed for each empty barrel.  
[*][b]Drill[/b] — Muskets: +18% movement speed while aiming, unlocks advanced stances.  
[*][b]Shoot to Kill[/b] — Balls stun enemies, slowing them by 25% for 5 seconds.  
[*][b]Elusiveness[/b] — Shoves: +30% shove power, less stamina cost.  
[*][b]Marathoner[/b] — +15% sprint speed, less stamina cost.  
[*][b]Flanking[/b] — Curved weapons: +10% attack speed, unlocks the advanced Group Attack.  
[/list]  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/7b749c71423b11dce2bbd8c073d90a5fe3b2a013.gif[/img]
Here’s how the Group Attack changes with the Flanking perk. Three swings instead of two.  
[hr][/hr]  
[h2]Items[/h2]  
As mentioned earlier, we’ve reworked almost every item in the game:  
[list]  
[*]All weapons and damage recalculated. Length and curvature alone no longer grant bonuses — their power depends on your perk choices.  
[*]Armor standardized: protection depends on material only, no penalties, and crits can’t be blocked.  
[*]Critical mechanics reworked: everyone has a base crit chance, but bonuses are rare. Crits are now rare but deadly.  
[*]Amulets: unified duration, no penalties or incompatibilities, new mechanics added.  
[*]Potions rebalanced, with new recipes and effects.  
[*]Ammo and crafting revised, paper cartridges now require rare resources.  
[*]Firearms fully reworked. They only shine in the hands of characters built for them — no more “early-game win button.”  
[/list]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/6f26abafe71ebca428a11c1a4847ef92abb5420c.png[/img]
[hr][/hr]  
[h2]New Personal Perks[/h2]  
[h3]Trees and Archetypes[/h3]  
The old system had a few “god-tier” perks surrounded by a pile of useless ones. Some didn’t even work (like the accuracy bonus).  

Now perks are organized into larger [b]archetypes[/b], each with its own playstyle:  
[list]  
[*][b]Musketeer[/b] — firearms, bayonets, ammo, and weapon swap speed.  
[*][b]Soldier[/b] — health pool, Heavy weapons, crowd control.  
[*][b]Duelist[/b] — glass cannon, reach, crits.  
[*][b]Pirate[/b] — area damage, Medium weapons, wider attack arcs.  
[*][b]Adventurer[/b] — social perks, rare weapons, crafting and looting.  
[*][b]Mastery[/b] — focused on specific weapon Descriptors like Heavy, Curved or Multi-Shot. In other words, tailoring perks to your favorite weapon.  
[/list]  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/3a8923a5649cbf74dfac0879278be9a422c7cde4.png[/img]
Combat fundamentals have changed as well: new mechanics and attack types added. No more skipping animations with a block. Feints are gone. Guard breaks now cause different stun animations, with backstabs being the most dangerous.  
[hr][/hr]  
[h2]Progression[/h2]  
The old system was too slow and grindy. Here’s what’s new:  
[list]  
[*]Perk costs cut in half (or even more).  
[*]Perk points earned more often (up to 2 per rank).  
[*]Perk costs vary: 1 to 3 points.  
[/list]  
As a result, players can master about 2.5 trees: either two archetypes fully or a unique hybrid build.  
[hr][/hr]  
[h2]Buildcrafting[/h2]  
The principle: cheap perks are universal, expensive perks are powerful but situational.  
Some perks can be combined across trees to create hybrid builds.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/7ccf044580bbebfa3aa8789dd2c9854a5a7b6aac.gif[/img]
Nothings stops Soldier from having some sweet Duelist moves.

Example hybrid-builds:  
- [b]Gunslinger-Swordsman[/b] — clears enemies at range, then dives in with AoE.  
- [b]Alchemist-Shooter[/b] — stacks power through items, crafting and social perks.  

We’re excited to see your guides — there may be at least eight builds… or infinite!  
[hr][/hr]  
[h2]Build Example: Rank 10 Pirate[/h2]  

We’ll start with the [b]Accountant[/b] background — it comes with a Machete right away.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/8a7ffd86ea82cb906ae921890fcfdd60c9c23143.png[/img]
By rank 10 you’ll have around 20 perk points.  

[list]  
[*]First 3 points — [b]Endurance[/b] and [b]Marathoner[/b].  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/230ef2c2e78afd527d5d93ae95b21b2d0652b84a.png[/img]
[*]Next 4 points — [b]Dragoon[/b], [b]Reach[/b], [b]Ottoman Grip[/b]. Together that’s +28% DPS.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/abc94efbc7bf9b553d62f9c1b7d3fc86ebe882e5.png[/img]
[*]Then grab [b]Flanking[/b] and [b]Saber Whirlwind[/b] for crowd fights.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/8dfa05573d295eb9b9405627027bb5882f3fd96f.png[/img]
[*]Final 7 points — [b]Rising Energy[/b], [b]Perfect Balance[/b], [b]Core Defense[/b], [b]Rising Health[/b].  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/362ba8e8c99a5457f804533688aee28fc24031cb.png[/img]
[/list]  
The result: a build perfect for large-scale battles, including the fight with Blackwood on the Caymans.  
[hr][/hr]  

[h2]Equipment[/h2]  
[list]  
[*]Weapons: start with the Machete, later upgrade to Scimitar, Storta, Shamshir, or Gallowsblade. Finding a better weapon would be easier since Accountants tend to find better loot in treasure chests.
[*]Armor: pieces with the [b]Tailored[/b] Descriptor (e.g., Leather Belt or Wicker Armor, + Attack Speed).  
[*]Hats: [b]Cavalier Hat[/b] (gain stamina on kill + even faster Group Attacks).  
[*]Potions: [b]Squall[/b] for more Attack Speed.  
[*]Amulets:  
- [b]Widowmaker[/b] (+damage to Group Attacks).  
- [b]Ngombo Shield[/b] (if you don’t have Wicker Armor).  
- [b]El Trozo[/b] (+2.5% movement speed per each Pagan amulet/ward).  
[/list]  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/8b03178e52b7c2b2f7a9a01c7a56991148298127.png[/img]
This is the perfect setup for tackling all mid-game content. And it's only one option of the many.
See y'all you soon.

[h2]Q&A[/h2]
[b]Joruba[/b]'s back again, folks. Taking the microphone from Kirill to answer your questions. I've already covered some questions personally in [url=https://discord.gg/caribbeanlegend]Discord[/url], but the most pressing and interesting ones made it here.

[i]The questions below came from:[/i]

flashdeck, U1993, Qorben, Mr Gualtieri, Mr. Goodman, Maksim, Sea Wolf, Honest Merchant, Wazar, Sarevok, Reider, Captain Fadey, Vanish, Frazzle, DimkaSuperStaR, GunpowderHater, macio460, Hawx, dolken0291, Escorpion, Lucy Okada, Ahoy, Sellec, Guarwo, Vokshus, Dimchik, KingOrren, Rizen, kacpermalinowski007, PZh, 4Za-V9, Ariel, Inner Observer, Мастер Течи.

Might have missed someone, sorry for that.

[hr][/hr]

[b]Question:[/b] Will there be a rework of how the maps work? Currently they don't do much.
[b]Answer:[/b] In [b]1.6[/b] the player's fleet speeds up in regions of which they have a map. If, of course, the corresponding naval perk is unlocked.

[b]Question:[/b] Are there plans to expand the global map — new islands, settlements?
[b]Answer:[/b] Not in this game. But we might add Old Providence island.

[b]Question:[/b] Is a radical rework of fencing planned on the current engine?
[b]Answer:[/b] Depends on what you consider a "radical rework". In version [b]1.6[/b] land combat plays completely differently, and you'll have to relearn everything.

[b]Question:[/b] What's the current status on the story mode for Diego?
[b]Answer:[/b] That's a 2016 meme. But seriously, there's almost no chance.

[b]Question:[/b] Will there be an official mod-kit with utilities and documentation?
[b]Answer:[/b] Possibly, after version [b]2.0[/b].

[b]Question:[/b] How will trade and economy develop in future patches?
[b]Answer:[/b] This is big. Much needs to be redone from scratch. For example, making the game to "see" which goods were bought or stolen where.

We're aiming for the Mount & Blade series experience. I always loved freeplaying in the early game there with a minimal squad, earning money in various ways and spending everything on buying enterprises. At some point money started making money, and you could afford an army. Amazing feeling, and I want to reproduce it in our game.

We planned to implement purchasing merchant stands already in [b]1.6[/b], but with a heavy heart, I decided to postpone it. For now, we're carefully adjusting the economy to increase the value of money in the game. It's not about hardcore, it's about not making hundreds of thousand of pesos instantly and with little effort. Where is fun in that?

[list]
[*] Increased the usefulness of the "Trading" skill.
[*] Made loot less rich.
[*] Removed cheaty trade routes completely.
[*] Removed aggressive demand goods.
[*] Made deposits less profitable.
[/list]

[b]Question:[/b] Is it possible to explain the logic behind the new ship balance?
[b]Answer:[/b] Due to how the bearing angle is currently implemented, our original design only works in tactical sailing mode. Once we solve this, the ship balance will work as intended. I think.

Generally the logic is rather simple:
[list]
[*] A raider with fore-and-aft sails can easily defeat one merchant.
[*] But if you conduct the attack poorly — the second merchant will surely escape downwind.
[*] And if there's also an escort of warriors — you'll be the one escaping.
[/list]

[b]Question:[/b] Is a rework of Vitality and Hull Degradation mechanics planned?
[b]Answer:[/b] The second has already been cut, then we'll cut the first too. Same goes for a few other useless mechanics and skills.

[b]Question:[/b] What about Charles de Maure's storyline? Epilogue, Mary?
[b]Answer:[/b] We'll wrap things up this year with some final content. It's [i]au revoir, Charles[/i] after that.

[b]Question:[/b] Will unique ships get their own traits?
[b]Answer:[/b] Unique ones — absolutely. Regular ships will get new traits too, especially warriors. We'll run a poll to ask for your ideas for new traits.

[b]Question:[/b] Is a rework of the sound system planned?
[b]Answer:[/b] Yes. Sound is half the game, in my opinion.

[b]Question:[/b] Can we get rid of those situations where the story prevents you from searching the captain's cabin after boarding?
[b]Answer:[/b] Yes. [b]1.6[/b] brings a new weight and encumbrance system.

[b]Question:[/b] Gamepad support?
[b]Answer:[/b] Planned. Most likely at the very end — when we finalize mechanics and interface.

[b]Question:[/b] Any plans to improve companions?
[b]Answer:[/b] Great question. We'd love to enhance the whole "admiral" gameplay. Like being able to:
[list]
[*] Send companions out raiding on their own.
[*] Have them run trade routes.
[*] Complete quests for you.
[/list]
It's a huge undertaking though. Not quite time for it yet, but it'll happen.

[b]Question:[/b] Can we capture and manage colonies?
[b]Answer:[/b] You can already capture them in sandbox mode. But real colony management would need city customizing, a rebuilt world map system, and an expanded threat system. That's endgame content, so it'll be a while. Might not happen at all — but we'd love to do it.

[b]Question:[/b] Adding letters of marque?
[b]Answer:[/b] Same deal as colonies.

[b]Question:[/b] Will Isla Mona be added to sandbox mode?
[b]Answer:[/b] We'll see next year. The quest was actually written with sandbox in mind from the start — all the dialogues for other heroes are made already.

[b]Question:[/b] Are you going to integrate any community mods?
[b]Answer:[/b] [i]Quality of Pirate's Life[/i] and [i]PerksReworked[/i] are getting the full treatment starting with [b]1.6[/b].

[b]Question:[/b] When can we stop having to start over with each patch?
[b]Answer:[/b] So far, only [b]1.5[/b] broke save files — and we warned about that almost a year ahead. The next one that definitely will require to start a new game is [b]2.0[/b]. Once you see what's in it, you'll get why.

[b]Question:[/b] When's Helen coming back as a playable character?
[b]Answer:[/b] It was my mistake, adding her in [b]1.3[/b] just to take away from you in [b]1.4[/b].

Getting the waifu back means:
[list]
[*] New animations for the updated controls.
[*] Brand new character model.
[*] Making sure hats, armor, lanterns, and muskets all work on her.
[/list]
I am sorry, we just don't have resources for that right now. 

[b]Question:[/b] Can you add two-handed weapon animations and make them a separate category?
[b]Answer:[/b] It's possible. But not happening.

[b]Question:[/b] Will there be cats in the game?
[b]Answer:[/b] As a cat person myself, I'd love that. We even had the feature planned and drafted. Maybe someday.

[b]Question:[/b] Any info on the next Ship's Pack DLC?
[b]Answer:[/b] Chapter four drops this year with one of the most requested ships in the game. You're gonna love it.

[b]Question:[/b] How about a new Dutch hero?
[b]Answer:[/b] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3545837950&searchtext=]Someone beat us to it.[/url] It's good.

[b]Question:[/b] Visible hats on officers? More stealth gear?
[b]Answer:[/b] No to the first, yes to the second starting in [b]1.6[/b].

[b]Question:[/b] When are we getting new graphics? New engine?
[b]Answer:[/b] Now that would be telling. ːcharles_happyː

[b]Question:[/b] Can we get cheaper ship storage?
[b]Answer:[/b] We're tying the prices to player's Trading skill. Not to mention, you will be able to keep the crew on the stored ship, at least temporarily.

[b]Question:[/b] How do you test new mechanics for balance?
[b]Answer:[/b]
[list]
[*] We start with Excel spreadsheets and formulas. I hate this part. Kirill loves it though.
[*] Internal playtesting — see if the idea actually works and the math checks out.
[*] Closed alphas and open betas — gather feedback from community and fine-tune from there.
[/list]
No other way to do it — the game's just too big and complex.

[b]Question:[/b] Any plans to expand social perks and skills?
[b]Answer:[/b] Starting in [b]1.6[/b], going full social build isn't just viable — it actually helps in combat too.

[hr][/hr]

[b]Summary:[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Patch 1.6[/b] open beta drops September 26.
[*] Starting the new game is NOT required.
[*] New DLC announcement coming next week.
[*] Wazar, Мастер Течи and GunpowderHater win this Q&A and get free copies.
[*] Thank you all for your great questions. It was fun and we should do it more often.
[/list]

That's it for today.
What we do — we do for you.
ːjollyrː

notes.title: Q&A, Mods of the Season and Teaser Image
notes.content:
[h1]Ahoy![/h1]

[b]On the menu:[/b]
[list]
[*] Starting a Q&A session
[*] Highlighting the best mods of the month
[*] Unveiling new content from patch 1.6
[/list]
[h2]Q&A[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Last week we released a dev diary showing a small, curved and fancy glimpse of the upcoming patch 1.6
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2230980/view/526478592467534463
Forty-four new perks, complete item overhaul, and more. We intentionally didn't reveal the details, but promised to make a separate post from the game designer if the diary got enough questions in the comments.
We got 9 pages of comments, so the post is definitely happening. But why stop there? We haven't chatted in a while, so the next [b]"Game Design Notes"[/b] will not only cover the mechanics, but also include a whole Q&A section.

We're collecting questions in the comments under this post, in the comments under the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2230980/view/526478592467534463?l=russian]dev diary[/url], and on our [url=https://discord.gg/s4prAwufpx]Discord server in the #qa channel[/url] until [b]September 12th.[/b]

I'll be answering the most interesting questions along with the game designer and other team members. [b]The authors of the three best questions will get keys for the DLC coming out at the end of September.[/b] That's the so-far-hidden pre-order DLC with three items. Though soon it'll have considerably more.
[h2]Mods of the Month[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
Q&A is all great and fun, but let's not forget that the third season of Steam Workshop just started recently. [b]In December, I'll award the best mod author $1000.[/b]
But right now I'd like to highlight some promising work from super talented creators.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3561262612&searchtext=
Super useful stuff from one of the Spanish localization authors. Next-gen and AAA gaming.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3515783993&searchtext=
The first mod with quest content from one of the BlackMark Studio team members. Translated into several languages and made, hopefully, outside of work hours. Want to see more of this.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3545837950
New hero for free play mode with a high level of polish matching the three base heroes. The author needs no introduction. You'll hear more about him from me this year.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3544584430
I'm against big ships and fleets in the game. So it's great that there are mods covering this need for the fairly large cohort of players who care about this sort of gameplay.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3539476021
Cool idea that improves one of our mechanics. Candidate for integration.

The second season had more mods than the first. The third [b]ALREADY[/b] has more than the second. I like this momentum, and I plan to do everything to keep things heating up.
 
Though not everything's perfect.
As before, I'm still disappointed by the lack of NSFW content.
Just keeping you posted.
[h2]Teaser picture[/h2]
[hr][/hr]
I believe that news in your Steam feed should provide value even if the topic might not interest you. 
Even if you don't care about the mod scene or surveys, you'll definitely like this.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/b4fbf3dad2d8fbb0f79f4e7fa596eb3b2d4c7311.png[/img]

notes.title: Dev Diary VII
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/0d834409e7d47464d1d281efeb441bc5462b90d6.jpg[/img]
[h1]Ahoy![/h1]

[list]
[*] Open beta for patch 1.6 launches September 26th.
[*] More changes than in 1.5
[*] Starting the new game will NOT be required.
[/list]
These past couple months our studio has been running at full throttle, collaborating with the best Steam Workshop creators, and just the other day we finally filled our last vacancy - a position I'd been trying to fill for a year and a half.

The result is an absolutely insane pace of development, so in the upcoming patch you'll see new mechanics, quests, ships, locations, and a massive QoL feature package that makes the game much more user firendly and fun.

But today we'll showcase only two new gameplay mechanics and one QoL feature. We won't go into detail yet - you'll see everything for yourselves soon enough.
[hr][/hr]
[b]Forty-four new perks.[/b] Caribbean Legend now features proper character building and replay value.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/46701b3eae663107906a6671cb6e886261353313.png[/img]

Off the top of my head, that's at least 8 completely different builds and countless hybrids. 
My favorite: sharpshooter-alchemist with exotic weapons. 
[hr][/hr]
Obviously, perk points are now distributed differently, and we've added several new combat, economy, and naval mechanics to the game. The biggest one - [b]complete overhaul of all items in the game[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/d4b336c6efc879a13a5cffa0f6a53b6ffe059901.png[/img]
Every item now has a set of descriptors or tags - properties that provide different bonuses and stack nicely with each other and with the new perks. In other words, the game now has item sets and huge room for experimentation. I doubt there are any useless items or crafting recipes left in the game now.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/2b745e46996ad0810c8f18de048037428195c892.png[/img]
Of course, we've written a new character generator, and every NPC - from sailors to bosses, purchases perks to match their equipment. Given how the combat system will change in 1.6, you'll need to learn to identify enemy archetypes and fight each one differently.
[hr][/hr]
Finally, my favorite new QoL mechanic in the game. Every UI element now [b]highlights and displays tooltips on mouse hover[/b]. Thanks to this feature, all interfaces in the game have suddenly become more convenient, and the game itself - clearer and more intuitive.

[img]https://media0.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTc5MGI3NjExMmpyOG5jemkxNnVkcTF3eGkydXFlcGt3a3Y1cGZhY2tqZ2o1ZmN1ayZlcD12MV9pbnRlcm5hbF9naWZfYnlfaWQmY3Q9Zw/H0irr0tbuqOqferwRm/giphy.gif[/img]
No more guessing what does what: just hover your cursor and get the full breakdown.

notes.title: Patch 1.5 and New DLC — OUT NOW
notes.content:
[h2]Ahoy![/h2]
[h3]On the menu:[/h3]
[list]
[*] The [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3549900/Caribbean_Legend__Ships_Pack_Part_3/]Ships Pack: Chapter 3[/url] DLC is out!
[*] Patch 1.5 is now available!
[*] [b]New game is mandatory![/b]
[*] If you want to continue your playthrough on version 1.4 or 1.3.5, then roll back the game version in your Steam library.
[*] Open beta 1.5 participants don't have to start a new game, but it's recommended.
[*] Disable any mods until Steam Workshop authors update them for the new version.
[*] The largest and most technically complex patch we have ever made.
[*] The main stars of this update are naval battles and the global map.
[*] Combat pacing in the early game has been improved — enemies no longer feel like damage sponges.
[*] Skill grind in early game has been resolved.
[*] Try it, master the new mechanics and share your impressions!
[/list]
[h2]DLC[/h2]
Purchase now and claim tons of rewards! This DLC is the richest in loot yet — just as a proper pirate tale should be.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3549900/Caribbean_Legend__Ships_Pack_Part_3/

For those who haven't been following, we remind you that the Ships Pack DLC series is dedicated to legendary captains and ships of the Caribbean Sea, connected by one tragic and even terrifying story. When the last, fifth Ships Pack comes out — the full picture will come together.

[h2]3D[/h2]
[h3]Three new decks[/h3]
We have replaced the scenes the player sees when boarding an enemy ship via a boat. The old ones were... well, outdated. Work will continue in the future: as with the boarding decks, we want the decks to match their ships more often.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/b0fa1de6e564da5c7126789335bbd3bde959fa44.png[/img]

[h3]New gun deck[/h3]
[h3]New crew's quarters[/h3]
[h3]New hold[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/702f2616b5b1ce50cf9d6cfa7b069602f1c0fe80.jpg[/img]

They turned out incredibly cool and visually stunning. Honestly, now we want to make ship content/events to motivate a player to spend more time in these locations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/d8eb4fe6f5a154430d0d80eec9533b19abd46ced.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/bfc2abcd5c8d6f00fe2a91430c60bdc8b91ea547.jpg[/img]

[h3]El Cazador[/h3]
The pirate hunter, pride of the Casa de Contratación and flagship of Spain's punitive fleet. The largest ship of all that we have made since the game's release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/085871cd7c80767836e26eacaedc1ebba25fd42b.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/4ed8ada0ab90c9512186e54a927ddba4d5e3d242.png[/img]

[h3]Brig[/h3]
A legendary ship type and the true king of speed in the new balance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/368763c983a139832e80d903d14a73e74f487c40.png[/img]
[h3]Ship improvements[/h3]
A number of old ships received many fixes: some got improved textures, others — better bow guns aiming. This work never stops.

[h3]New Diego[/h3]
[h3]New William[/h3]
[h3]League Armor[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/9b851f3962ce7be0098ae2ed265e31fb0bafc11e.png[/img]

Finally, all main characters’ outfits meet our new quality standard, and League Armor looks on par with the rest of the armors in the game.

[h2]Content[/h2]
[h3]Prologue[/h3]

We never liked the tutorial on Martinique, mainly because the player saw the most beautiful and cool side of the game only after half an hour or even later. The sea.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/1ffb64b0e7ad3aaa87cec8f33f4b90619deba8c6.jpg[/img]

As a result, Charles de Maure’s story received a small but exciting prologue on the pinnace “Ulysses.” Newcomers will enjoy the interactivity and clearer tutorial, while experienced players will find it interesting to see the main character from a different perspective.

And, if you haven’t figured it out yet, instead of an epilogue, we made a prologue.

[h3]Seven new quests[/h3]
Initially, we planned to add small events, so the player would make useful acquaintances in every city. A shipyard friend, an indebted innkeeper, a “favorite” waitress, and so on. But at some point, the events grew so much that they turned into full-fledged side quests.

It really brought freeplay to life, and the rewards... well, you’ll like them.
[h2]Character[/h2]
[h3]Exploration bonuses[/h3]
I really like the early stage of the game. What I don’t like that the game forces you to grind experience and officers.

Now the character receives bonuses for the first visit to certain locations, and navigation skill grows automatically on the global map. This is very useful in early game, works great with new side quests and colony secrets, and lets you roleplay as a trader or treasure hunter without having to grind navigation in storms or reload endlessly to recruit officers in taverns. 

Of course, after about the first 30 skill points, this progression slows down a lot and quickly becomes irrelevant, but the early game is no longer so “stifling,” and overall there’s less grind.

[h3]Melee weapon damage rebalance[/h3]

[b]Before:[/b]
[list]
[*] Damage sponges in early game and one-hit kills in end game;
[*] Unclear damage calculation — people had to look for guides and a weapon calculator mod.
[/list]
[b]Now:[/b]
[list]
[*] Fair damage in early game, rewarding progression in end game;
[*] Weapon damage stats provide clear picture, especially in mid-game;
[/list]
Simply put, fights are now faster and more dangerous. There’s less tedium, critical hits work more honestly, and melee with muskets is no longer OP — its damage now depends on the Firearms skill.

Hidden stats like weapon length/curvature, balance, and attack type modifiers no longer play the main role in damage calculations. Weapon skill, amulets, and blade damage do. However, if you’re an experienced player, nothing stops you from maxing damage by using the right attacks with the right weapon.

[h3]Small rebalance of backgrounds[/h3]
PIRATES parameters were changed for all backgrounds. The “T” parameter is now almost the same for everyone, and each background got a nine in one profile stat. In addition, targeted skill tweaks were made, so the difference between backgrounds is now more pronounced.

[h3]Stealth check simplified[/h3]
Another plus for free exploration and our desperate fight against save scumming. Fooling enemies (especially on small ships) is now easier.
[h2]Sea[/h2]
[h3]Ship rebalance and trait system[/h3]
We’ve talked a lot about this innovation and even dedicated separate dev diaries to it.

[b]In short:[/b]
[list]
[*] Ships are now divided into: [b]Warriors[/b], [b]Raiders[/b], [b]Traders[/b]. Each type is distinct and gets access to different [b]traits[/b].
[*] A trait is a unique feature of a specific ship. Examples of traits can be found in the screenshots below.
[*] There’s one more ship type — [b]multipurpose[/b] ships. They have no notable advantages or disadvantages, can’t have traits, but their upgrades at shipyards give more significant stat bonuses.
[*] Average hold size, max crew, and gun weight have been noticeably increased. Since all this determines speed, combat, and trading, you can confidently tailor any ship to your needs and playstyle.
[*] Added Rate 7 and fully developed Rate 6. Sixth Rate now requires only 5 navigation skill points, so progression is smoother and finding a navigator is no longer mandatory early on.
[*] Ships now differ much more within their rate, and the difference between rates is even greater. Choosing a ship is always a compromise, and changing class is a big event.
[*] The off-bow angle stat is now more important. The fastest ships in the game are square-riggers, but fore-and-aft rigged ships are much more flexible and less dependent on wind whims.
[*] The AI now knows how to use its optimal wind angle and chooses its course based on its rigging.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/73858e55cd81500e0faa1c30f1a433e137d31ab5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/508d0dc71b5d49c58542dd57cb057bc3b071319d.png[/img]

[h3]Two new gun calibers and gun rebalance[/h3]
We’ve added two new guns: 8 and 18-punders — for better progression and to highlight the best guns for early and mid-game. Overall, all guns gradually improve in stats, the choice between them is more of a compromise, and encounters with Warrior ships have become very dangerous.

[h3]Fleet Power and threat system[/h3]
[i]“Let’s make the Nations Window more useful?”[/i]
Here’s what came out of it:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/bb9ea45467ff31445f533a7e65e0cc0852cd07fa.png[/img]

[b]Fleet Power and Threat Level concepts introduced.[/b]
The Caribbean now pays close attention to the player’s ship or fleet, evaluating type, rate, number, and condition of ships. The weak are hunted, the strong are feared.
[list]
[*] If you anger a nation, it will assign you a threat level and send hunters after you. If your Fleet Power is higher than the threat level, the enemy won’t risk attacking, and you can move safely on the global map.
[*] If your fleet was recently battered in battle or its power was always below the threat level, expect visitors.
[*] Sea encounters, many radiant quests and some story quests have been reworked for this system. Fleet composition, power, and hold contents were set manually for each case.
[*] You can protect yourself from Threat Level 1 just by sailing a good Warrior ship of Rate 5 or hiring a companion. A Trader will have to mount heavy guns or hire an escort. Threat Level 5 can only be countered by assembling a fleet of line ships.
[*] Unlike nations, threat from pirates increases over time. Whether you want it or not, the world will become more dangerous.
[*] Diplomats have been reworked: each request reduces the threat level by one.
[*] The “Terror of the Seas” perk can now be unlocked without leveling sea skills. It significantly increases your Fleet Power.
[*] The “Black Mark” ward now also works differently, increasing your Fleet Power.
[*] During sea encounters, you’ll now see a battle outcome prediction. Your Fleet Power is compared to the enemy’s.
[*] We’ll add this to the beta very soon, but at certain threat levels, nations will send unique bounty hunters. In story mode, it will be “Cazador,” and in freeplay, you may be hunted by “Chimera,” “Griffondor,” and “Meifeng.” [b]This is not only a way to get quest ships in freeplay, but also unique loot from officers.[/b]
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/62947b7cb6a024b88ad216d105fab5588a4ac8e2.png[/img]

[h3]New first-person aiming at sea[/h3]
The update to musket and pistol shooting has refreshed the game and brought a whole new layer to the combat system. [b]We did the same for naval battles.[/b]

Previously, naval first-person shooting was clunky and boring, but now you have full control of the guns, can target masts, sails, rudders, and fort guns. Roll, mouse speed, character skills, and above all, your own player skill affect aiming speed and accuracy.

You no longer need to find a gunner to fight effectively at sea. Feel full control over artillery, enjoy new smoke and fire effects and gun sounds. The more you practice, the better you get, and everyone who’s tried it says the same: you won’t want to go back to the old system.

But enough talk — see for yourself.

https://youtu.be/RZRegqBs6fk

[h3]Punitive fleets[/h3]
At high threat levels, nations will send their best hunters after you.

In Story Mode: “El Cazador”.
In Sandbox Mode: “El Cazador”, “Meifeng”, “Chimera”, and “Griffondor”.

These are extremely dangerous enemies — true world map bosses. But the rewards are well worth it: unique gear, and a chance to recruit officers and ships from Charles’s storyline.

For the first time, freeplay mode offers a clear advantage over story mode — for example, you can now get both Longway and Charlie in the same run.

[h3]Sieges[/h3]
We've reworked fort siege mechanics: now wall bombardment deals proper damage to forts. This makes first-rate ships a real force in sieges, allows smaller squadrons to participate more effectively, and makes AI assaults against forts more dangerous. Also, using the new first-person aiming mode now deals significantly more damage to forts — targeting wall cannons not only disables them but also causes splash damage to the surrounding walls.

[h3]Slave Traders[/h3]
We've added a new type of encounter on the global map - slave traders. This is a well-guarded convoy carrying a cargo of slaves. In terms of rarity, it appears about as often as a crown expedition. A foundation for the future faction system.

[h2]UI[/h2]
[h3]Interface optimization[/h3]
Trade, inventory and character windows no longer lag. You can add all items in the game to yourself, it will load smoothly and quickly.

[h3]Improved camera at sea[/h3]
You can now view the ship better and closer. We’ve also taken the first steps toward a full free camera mode.

[h3]Officer and passenger tabs[/h3]
Officers and passengers with prisoners are now separated into different tabs in the character and inventory windows. No more endless scrolling through thirty prisoners to assign an officer.
 
[h3]Crew hiring[/h3]
The crew hiring window has been reworked. You now clearly see all necessary information and all bonuses and penalties. The formula for calculating the number of recruits has been reworked. No more running around all the colonies to assemble your crew. In late game, with all bonuses, you can hire up to 300 people from one tavern.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/91fa6bc6d53bb4045bf850ba1a600496371ec9fa.png[/img]

[h3]News feed[/h3]
Added another button to the main menu for important news and messages. Be sure to read it, or we’ll deduct social points from you.

[h3]Additional notifications[/h3]
Added several new notifications: goods spoiled by rats, musket volley effectiveness, changes in relations with smugglers, and so on.

[h3]Improved control settings[/h3]
We've continued expanding the control customization options. Now any player, whether right-handed or left-handed, can configure control keys without limitations to suit their needs. This may seem like a small thing, but making it possible on our engine was no easy task.

[h3]General improvements[/h3]
Readability and fonts in various windows have been improved, and names on the global map are now displayed more clearly.

[h2]Miscellaneous[/h2]
[h3]New random[/h3]
Here’s the thing... RNG in the game always worked very poorly and often got stuck. Many generated quest options never appeared at all. We rewrote the generation method and now random works as it should. If you’re used to catching “Holy Water” drops to run to the beach for treasure chests — today is your bad day.

[h3]Walking in block[/h3]
The last brick in the new controls. The character can now move with an active block. You can now safely change position, then use sprint to break through the enemy line and make a couple of headshots from afar.

[h3]Swimming sprint[/h3]
Tired of endless swims on Justice Island? Now they’re a bit less tedious. The character can now sprint in water. I am sorry, I don't know the word for it.

[h3]New effects[/h3]
We’ve improved effects like fire, smoke, and so on. There are still some minor tweaks left, but it looks great. Especially well combined with the new naval shooting.

[h3]New sounds[/h3]
Sounds have been added for all calibers in the game. Every gun now “sings” in its own way.

[h3]Italian localization[/h3]
Pizza time! Grazie mille, MoonDragon!

[h3]Additions and fixes for all languages in the game[/h3]

[h3]11 new achievements[/h3]

[h3]A lot of various bugs and issues have been fixed, and even more new ones have been added.
[/h3]

And... that's all for now!
Try out the patch, grab the DLC, and leave us a review — bright and blue like the Caribbean Sea! ːsteamthumbsupː

[h2]Content[/h2]
[h3]Prologue[/h3]

We never liked the tutorial on Martinique, mainly because the player saw the most beautiful and cool side of the game only after half an hour or even later. The sea.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/a9430524470fe7a9c8ca274425023f0c2403bb8f.jpg[/img]

As a result, Charles de Maure’s story received a small but exciting prologue on the pinnace “Ulysses.” Newcomers will enjoy the interactivity and clearer tutorial, while experienced players will find it interesting to see the main character from a different perspective.

And, if you haven’t figured it out yet, instead of an epilogue, we made a prologue.

[h3]Seven new quests[/h3]
Initially, we planned to add small events, so the player would make useful acquaintances in every city. A shipyard friend, an indebted innkeeper, a “favorite” waitress, and so on. But at some point, the events grew so much that they turned into full-fledged side quests.

It really brought freeplay to life, and the rewards... well, you’ll like them.
[h2]Character[/h2]
[h3]Exploration bonuses[/h3]
I really like the early stage of the game. What I don’t like that the game forces you to grind experience and officers.

Now the character receives bonuses for the first visit to certain locations, and navigation skill grows automatically on the global map. This is very useful in early game, works great with new side quests and colony secrets, and lets you roleplay as a trader or treasure hunter without having to grind navigation in storms or reload endlessly to recruit officers in taverns. 

Of course, after about the first 30 skill points, this progression slows down a lot and quickly becomes irrelevant, but the early game is no longer so “stifling,” and overall there’s less grind.

[h3]Melee weapon damage rebalance[/h3]

[b]Before:[/b]
[list]
[*] Damage sponges in early game and one-hit kills in end game;
[*] Unclear damage calculation — people had to look for guides and a weapon calculator mod.
[/list]
[b]Now:[/b]
[list]
[*] Fair damage in early game, rewarding progression in end game;
[*] Weapon damage stats provide clear picture, especially in mid-game;
[/list]
Simply put, fights are now faster and more dangerous. There’s less tedium, critical hits work more honestly, and melee with muskets is no longer OP — its damage now depends on the Firearms skill.

Hidden stats like weapon length/curvature, balance, and attack type modifiers no longer play the main role in damage calculations. Weapon skill, amulets, and blade damage do. [h3]Stealth check simplified[/h3]
Another plus for free exploration and our desperate fight against save scumming. Fooling enemies (especially on small ships) is now easier.
[h2]Sea[/h2]
[h3]Ship rebalance and trait system[/h3]
We’ve talked a lot about this innovation and even dedicated separate dev diaries to it.

[b]In short:[/b]
[list]
[*] Ships are now divided into: [b]Warriors[/b], [b]Raiders[/b], [b]Traders[/b]. Each type is distinct and gets access to different [b]traits[/b].
[*] A trait is a unique feature of a specific ship. Examples of traits can be found in the screenshots below.
[*] There’s one more ship type — [b]multipurpose[/b] ships. They have no notable advantages or disadvantages, can’t have traits, but their upgrades at shipyards give more significant stat bonuses.
[*] Average hold size, max crew, and gun weight have been noticeably increased. Since all this determines speed, combat, and trading, you can confidently tailor any ship to your needs and playstyle.
[*] Added Rate 7 and fully developed Rate 6. Sixth Rate now requires only 5 navigation skill points, so progression is smoother and finding a navigator is no longer mandatory early on.
[*] Ships now differ much more within their rate, and the difference between rates is even greater. Choosing a ship is always a compromise, and changing class is a big event.
[*] The off-bow angle stat is now more important. The fastest ships in the game are square-riggers, but fore-and-aft rigged ships are much more flexible and less dependent on wind whims.
[*] The AI now knows how to use its optimal wind angle and chooses its course based on its rigging.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/508d0dc71b5d49c58542dd57cb057bc3b071319d.png[/img]

[h3]Two new gun calibers and gun rebalance[/h3]
We’ve added two new guns: 8 and 18-punders — for better progression and to highlight the best guns for early and mid-game. Overall, all guns gradually improve in stats, the choice between them is more of a compromise, and encounters with Warrior ships have become very dangerous.

[h3]Fleet Power and threat system[/h3]
[i]“Let’s make the Nations Window more useful?”[/i]
Here’s what came out of it:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/bb9ea45467ff31445f533a7e65e0cc0852cd07fa.png[/img]

[b]Fleet Power and Threat Level concepts introduced.[/b]
The Caribbean now pays close attention to the player’s ship or fleet, evaluating type, rate, number, and condition of ships. The weak are hunted, the strong are feared.

[*] If you anger a nation, it will assign you a threat level and send hunters after you. If your Fleet Power is higher than the threat level, the enemy won’t risk attacking, and you can move safely on the global map.

[*] During sea encounters, you’ll now see a battle outcome prediction. Your Fleet Power is compared to the enemy’s.
[*] We’ll add this to the beta very soon, but at certain threat levels, nations will send unique bounty hunters. In story mode, it will be “Cazador,” and in freeplay, you may be hunted by “Chimera,” “Griffondor,” and “Meifeng.” [b]This is not only a way to get quest ships in freeplay, but also unique loot from officers.[/b]

notes.title: Mod of the Season
notes.content:
[h2]Ahoy![/h2]
In February, we added mod support and launched a program to support the best authors.
The winner of the first season - [b]PerksReworked[/b] mod by mega-talented Pvt. Joker!
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3439902769

An amazing work where the author not only added new perks but also organically integrated them into the game, preserving the style of the original. It looks as if it was always part of the game, and I know many people who no longer play without this mod.

Besides [b]PerksReworked[/b], Private Joker has created several other awesome works, some of which I'm even considering adding to the project. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/suddenbear/myworkshopfiles/?appid=2230980][b]You can find them here[/b][/url].

BlackMark Studio sincerely congratulates the winner, promises not to ban him anymore (at least in the relatively near future), and [b]awards $1000 of well-deserved loot.[/b] ːbootyː

We'd also like to mention [b]Winarik, Sem, TemplarFulga, Gregg, and Alex Rendel[/b] for their works that greatly enlivened this season and enriched our Steam Workshop. Thank you, guys.

What's next? The second season opens! The rules are the same: the author of the most popular mod on Steam Workshop from April 20 to August 20 will receive fame, honor, and $1000. Only the original author who uploaded the mod to the platform can become the winner.
Good luck!

[h3]What's up with 1.5?[/h3]
The team is in total crunch, but we'll finish the open beta by the end of May. A new game will definitely be required, but you can continue your playthrough on 1.4 by rolling back the version at any time.
We've significantly revised our plans and postponed much of what was planned, but it's worth it. The main stars of patch 1.5 will be naval battles and the global map, and our task is to bring back a sense of novelty and exploration to these most important layers of the game. In many ways, you'll have to rediscover the game.

The team currently has so much work that this month we definitely won't manage developer diaries or "Game Designer's Notes," but we can't help sharing some good stuff.

Of course, everything below is not final and will be changed and refined.

notes.title: Patch 1.4 and New DLC — OUT NOW
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/850a2d769d247ffbfd66a9e0cf4d546ab496754e.png[/img][h2]Ahoy![/h2]

[h3]What's New:[/h3]

[*] Plenty of new features and bug fixes included.
[*] No need to start a new game.
[/list]
[h2]Ships Pack: Part 2[/h2]
Grab the DLC, and enjoy an exciting story with plenty of loot!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3549890/Caribbean_Legend__Ships_Pack_Part_2/

For those who haven't been following along, the Ships Pack series features legendary captains and vessels of the Caribbean, all interconnected through one tragic and rather terrifying storyline. Once the fifth and final Ships Pack releases, the complete saga will be revealed.

[h3][b]What's Included:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] A brand new global map event available in both story and free play modes
[*] Albert Blackwood's visits to French ports across the Lesser Antilles, where you can gather rumors and encounter the captain himself
[*] Unique items – including a legendary arquebus and a useful talisman
[*] An epic battle against a seasoned military commander and his loyal crew
[*] A fast and powerful snow ship with unique effects
[*] Five new achievements to unlock

[list]
[*] The arquebus can be upgraded – search for parts in treasure chests
[*] Blackwood cannot be intercepted at sea

[/list]

https://youtu.be/gK0jZaD3cXw?si=4w7wQD5c5H2uvYQ_

[h2]Patch 1.4[/h2]
No need to start a new game, and for those who prefer to stay on 1.3.5 - it will always remain available in a separate branch. 

We've discussed 1.4 in detail in previous updates; it includes many features that were originally planned for 1.5. Most importantly - no more tank controls, 4 new localizations (still in beta), and a wave of content and features.

[b]Bad news for beta testers[/b]: I'm afraid you'll need to read through the change list once more - it's grown quite a bit over the past two weeks. ːrofl_pirateː

Details below.

[h3]What's New:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]New Snow Ship Model[/b]
Since we've added a unique snow in the [i]Ships Pack: Part 2[/i] DLC, it would be strange not to update the common snow ship as well. Completely redesigned model with several skins to choose from. Snow ships frequently appear in caravans, so this will definitely breathe new life into the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/5cc4f21ebf294be2490e604b4f672b0bbe1fd9c6.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/b458fc5aee7f02d31fd8418337b5fa6c17661bec.jpg[/img]

[*] [b]Controls 1.0[/b]
In short: the new control system is ready in its basic form. You can now move along all axes, switch to sprint, jump with weapons in hand, aim manually, have full camera control, and break through enemy formations. If you haven't seen the video below, check it out - though the current in-game version is already much more refined.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I2RROaiNY9c

The development of the new control system cost a lot of money and man-hours, but I'd gladly invest just as much again - I'm really eager to see Controls 2.0. We've sorted out the shooting. Time to tackle fencing? And gamepad support is now on the table too.

[i][b]Based on beta feedback, we've fixed numerous bugs and issues.[/b][/i]

[i][b]Everything comes at a price: Helen McArthur is temporarily unavailable as a main character.[/b][/i]

[*] [b]Weapon Switching While Moving[/b]
You can now draw and put away weapons, switch between musket and saber while on the move. Seems like a small thing, but it fundamentally changes the gameplay. With this addition, the controls have finally become fully dynamic, and it really shines in the new boarding scenes where players can combine jumps, aiming, pushing, and quick switching between musket and melee weapons.

[*] [b]Dynamic Crosshair[/b]
Aiming with handheld firearms is now more dynamic. The crosshair highlights when you're aiming, hitting, and eliminating enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/4424c2a442d347141aa7a7f9d962d1b862e1caa6.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/416136b33091c185a63ad7f26971bff04efeab31.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]Camera Sensitivity No Longer Depends on Frame Rate[/b]
An old problem that caused jerky camera movement and stuttering visuals. Now aiming and camera movement are much smoother, even in acceleration mode. 

[i][b]If your mouse sensitivity differs significantly from the standard 1600 DPI, we recommend adjusting the camera in the new settings.[/b][/i]

[*] [b]Improved Key Rebinding[/b]
For Steam players, having full control over key bindings is crucial. Not to mention left-handed players who literally struggled to play our game. While I can't say development in this area is completely finished, I hope the control customization now meets modern standards and player expectations.

[*] [b]Improved German Localization (beta)[/b]
[*] [b]Added Spanish, French, and Polish Localizations (beta)[/b]
I'm not ready to announce official support for these languages yet, but work on localizations continues. For example, people are already actively working on Italian, Hungarian, and Ukrainian translations. It's a long process, and all participants in this [url=https://discord.gg/WCu6As6DRM]Discord server[/url] are heroes. Join in if you'd like to help.

[i][b]Over the past two weeks, the translations have been significantly improved. Please remember that the game does not yet officially support these new languages, and work on them continues.[/b][/i]

[*] [b]Spanish Voice Acting Added[/b]
What can I say - bravo to [b]Jtem and the Spanish translation team[/b]. Best community in the world. Thank you, muchachos.

[*] [b]New Grapeshot Logic[/b]
How did it work before? Players would target one enemy, and if grapeshot was loaded, all enemies around the target would take damage. Now the grapeshot actually fires pellets. We've added spread parameters and the number of projectiles per load. By using different weapons and ammunition, you can either cover the entire deck or turn your swivel gun into a proper "trench sweeper" by sending dozens of pellets at a single enemy right in front of you. Interestingly, during testing, we replaced the pellets with church candles to make it easier to track pellet spread and test the mechanics. As a result, by the end of battle, every battlefield started to look like a church.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/c3bb49650f140146fda688752a80db4743f77de9.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/d814f659d2c2160c1c6a429b3a2687d0b86ef857.png[/img]

[*] [b]Another Boarding Scene[/b]
We've added a Corvette VS Pinnace scene that triggers when at least one of the boarding participants is a third-rate merchant ship. With this, the 5th, 4th, and 3rd rates are complete, and we're taking a break from boarding scenes. We have big plans for the second and first rates, and those ships take longer to create. By that time, I hope the controls will have evolved enough that we can implement full vertical gameplay, fortification assaults, and turn the large ship scenes into proper battlefields.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/31d36e2a4cad65255bd8b5605ca793b46d356372.png[/img]
[*] [b]New Charles de Maure Model[/b]
The realization that we urgently needed new models for the main characters hit me exactly when I saw how terrible everything looked up close during aiming. Moreover, all the equipment (armor, weapons, hats) is made in very high quality, making the old, blurry main character model really stand out. And frankly, we're tired of that green coat with cuffs. Future plans include clothing changes, customization options, and new models for Willie, Diego, and Helen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/04f45f83af84c49302f407b7d6cf89e24411b7c0.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]Hats[/b]
Adding hats and helmets has been on our wishlist for a long time. The game really needed another category of loot and additional character customization. You can find hats through the story, but most can be discovered in treasure chests. Some hats have very powerful bonuses, but don't limit yourself. Fashion rules the world. Wear what you like. In the future, I hope we can add belts and helmets. Then you'll be able to fully customize your characters. I think that's important. The bad news: for now, only Charles and Diego can visibly wear hats.

[i][b]Beta testers suggested a great idea, so Charlie Prince's hat is now given to the player during the pirate drinking session as a gift from Marcus Tirex and his gang.[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/fd0177f48fea14f02bf50168024948d00ddebaef.png[/img]
[*] [b]Treasure System Overhaul[/b]
The contents of treasure chests now resemble what a real person might have hidden, and they drop with more fair randomization. Level up your luck skill, make treasure hunting your profession - and the game will reward you. Free play mode enthusiasts are especially lucky: you can now obtain all story mode rewards through treasures. Kirill explained the mechanics in detail in his latest dev diary. In short - treasures have become significantly more valuable.

[b][i]After reviewing your beta feedback, we've doubled the number of notes in treasures, improved balance and progression, removed unnecessary half-maps from the game, and prohibited their activation when a complete map is already in the inventory.
[/i][/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2230980/view/525336841073722793?l=english
[*] [b]New Port Royal[/b]
Creating locations on this engine, especially open ones, is hellish work. That's why I sincerely thank [b]karlik.nos[/b] for helping us progress with updating colonial capitals in the game. We adapted his work to match the game's style and finally released it. Two more to go: Havana and Capsterville.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/400f39d2b4305ea342ee5fcfa5c073dbf078d892.jpg[/img]
[*] [b]New Interior[/b]
We've added another location - a wine cellar. It was originally planned for one of the new scenes in 1.5, but we found use for it now. A small thing, but nice.

[*] [b]"Mystery of Port Royal" Event[/b]
[*] [b]"Mystery of Willemstad" Event[/b]
Locations should not only look decent and service the player and their ship but also tell stories. Until recently, there wasn't much to explore in the game. We're starting to fix that. Next up - Le François and Saint-Pierre.

[i][b]Thanks to your feedback, we completely rewrote Port Royal's story and improved the hints in Willemstad. "Mystery of Port Royal" now also gets a unique reaction from one of the hero's officers.[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/a8065b657eb1f5f5e6071619600f4eee29342f92.png[/img]
[*] [b]Bulk Purchase of Strategic Goods[/b]
If you've leveled up your trading skill, need lignum vitae, silk, ropes, or pitch, but don't have time, try negotiating with suppliers for large shipments and become a partner. Now it makes sense to return for each delivery on a specific day of the month.

[*] [b]Complete Overhaul of Special Effects[/b]
A new direction in our work. We've redesigned from scratch the effects for smoke, fire, explosions, blood, magic - almost everything. The old effects were from 2008, had only 4 frames, and a resolution of 512x512. The new ones have 16 frames and 2K resolution. There's still a lot of work to be done on fine-tuning and optimization, but I like the first version. It's a great way to improve the game's graphics and enhance combat visuals.

[i][b]Following the beta, we significantly improved the effects. The game now has truly impressive fire and smoke.[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/fbd83dd83a6d4b4d5e818bae0419145a9d7fc8d9.png[/img]

[*] [b]Improved Interior Graphics[/b]
[*] [b]Texture Refinements[/b]
[*] [b]Lighting Improvements[/b]
This workfront never stops. We're gradually refining various textures, adjusting ambient occlusion (AO) in interiors, improving lighting, and removing glare. Small steps, but the game is becoming more beautiful with each patch.

[*] [b]New Hand Firearm Sounds[/b]
We've improved shooting so significantly that it not only became overpowered but also demanded special attention. We've replaced all the shooting sounds: from loading to firing.

[i][b]Additionally, the final 1.4 version includes all new weapon, cannon, and battle sounds. Combat has become much more lively.[/b][/i]

[*] [b]Improved Body Searching[/b]
More convenient looting, especially for the new control system. When attempting to search an "empty" body, you'll get a quick and unobtrusive notification without opening the exchange window.

[*] [b]Removed Camera Restrictions in Boarding Scenes[/b]
Since we've finally replaced most of the boarding decks in the game, we can now afford the luxury of disabling camera restrictions during boarding. Just don't look up on the first and second-rank boarding decks. All for the better: one day we'll place sharpshooters on the fighting tops.

[*] [b]14 New Achievements[/b]

[*] [b]Steam Workshop Button in the Main Menu[/b]

[*] [b]Various Fixes[/b]
Bugs, spelling, crashes, exploits, refinements. There won't be a list - we still have chaos in this department. But I can say with certainty: today is better than yesterday, and tomorrow will be better than today.
Important note: added migration support for mod creators. Now you can configure your content so it doesn't require starting a new game.

[i][b]We've fixed beta errors too. For example, the inability to complete FtJR questline and stuck port carriers.[/b][/i]
[/list]

And... that's it for the day. Buy the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3549890/Caribbean_Legend__Ships_Pack_Part_2/]DLC[/url], leave reviews as blue as the Caribbean Sea, and collect all the notes in treasures. Thank you for playing! And my personal [b]huge[/b] thanks to beta testers, translators, and mod creators.

See you at sea.
ːjollyrː

The first one simply killed the game from the first seconds for a huge number of people, while the second severely limited left-handed players and simply didn't meet modern convenience standards.

Both problems are solved: the controls have become modern and dynamic, and keys can now be rebinded almost without limitations. And... is that all? Ready to release?

Not quite. As it turned out, while working on 1.5, we have already managed to complete many cool things that, moreover, don't require starting a new game. Let's throw them in too.

[h3]What's new:[/h3]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I2RROaiNY9c

The development of the new control system cost a lot of money and man-hours, but I'll gladly invest just as much again - because I really want to see Modern Controls 2.0. Since we've figured out shooting, I'd say it is time to reimagine fencing? Add gamepad support?

Now you can draw and put away weapons, switch between musket and saber and back while moving. Seems like a small thing, but it actually changes the game dramatically. With the addition of this feature, the controls have finally become fully dynamic, and it works especially well in new boarding scenes, where players can combine jumps, sprinting, aiming, pushing, and quick switching between musket and melee weapons.

[*] [b]Improved key rebinding[/b]

[*] [b]Improved German localization (beta)[/b]
[*] [b]Added Spanish, French, and Polish localizations (beta)[/b]

We've introduced new parameters of spread and the number of projectiles per charge. Or chose something in the middle perhaps? 

It's funny that during testing, we replaced the pellets with candles to make it easier to track the spread and test the mechanics. As a result, at the end of each battle, every battlefield started to look like a church.

This kind of work never stops. We're gradually improving various textures, adjusting ambient occlusion (AO) in interiors, improving lighting, and removing glare. Small steps, but the game is becoming more beautiful with each patch.

[h3]Mod of the Month[/h3]
It's been a month since we added modding support. Unfortunately, no [i]proper mods[/i] for Helen and Mary have been released during this time, but the community has still rolled out plenty of cool stuff.

notes.title: GD Notes #3. Treasure Hunting.
notes.content:
[h1]Ahoy![/h1]

Hoist the topsails, set course for the bay of creativity!
Greetings from Kirill, I'm delighted to meet you all once again.

In this dev diary, we'll talk about a mechanic that is expected and loved in every pirate game - treasure hunting.
It has long needed reworking and revision, and has probably been waiting for its time longer than all other mechanics combined.

[h2]The Issue[/h2]

Treasure hunting is a theme shrouded in romance, mystery, and a thirst for exploration, and the gameplay implementation should reflect this. Since we currently don't have the opportunity to rework the treasure hunting process itself, we'll be working on the content.

Now, the big question. What would you prefer to find in a hidden treasure after sailing halfway through the archipelago in search of it:

[*]Something valuable and immersive, telling a story and resembling what a real person might have hidden.

[b]OR[/b]

[*]Thirty cutlasses, twenty nails.

I'm more inclined towards the first option, but the game currently implements the second - and that's a problem. The treasure generation is too chaotic, and players can't influence it except by reloading before activating the map.
You might get lucky and find great items in your very first treasure, or you might dig up several treasures in a row and find only junk. Zero roleplay.

[h2]Treasure Generation[/h2]

Let's go step by step, starting from the moment you pick up a map.

Treasures are no longer a simple random number generator; now they're a [b]complex and intricate[/b] random number generator with a bunch of conditions.

When generating a treasure upon picking up a map, the game checks many parameters, including:
[list]
[*]Map level (whether it's a simple map or one assembled from halves)
[*]Luck skill
[*]Number of treasures you found so far
[*]Accountant perk check
[/list]
Based on these parameters, the boundaries of treasure tiers are calculated, after which a random one is selected.

Treasure tiers, in turn, determine the relative value of treasures and the list of items that can and cannot be generated in them. There are 15 tiers in total, and the set of items for each tier has been manually selected to look as immersive as possible.

Thus, treasure hunting transforms from a moderately useful side activity into a profession in which you can improve. The more treasures you find the more valuable they become. By enhancing your luck and taking a higher-level map, you can jump through several tiers at once.
The Accountant background becomes an ideal choice for finding better treasures, as it reaches high tiers much faster.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/bb5c7b92325e8cee17e922fa3176c09401f372b2.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/847cf09ca019e1e37e748c170bd4d59158bc68a5.png[/img]

Here's an example of a low-tier treasure and a high-tier one. Reaching high treasure tiers isn't easy, but the reward is worth it.

[h2]Content Generation[/h2]

As I mentioned above, each treasure tier has its own set of items for generation, but what are these items?

In general, treasure contents are divided into 4 sections. Within each section, a treasure has a certain number of slots that can be filled with items available at the current treasure tier, each with different probabilities.

Items are generated in such a way that treasures are as diverse as possible - getting 2 identical items from 2 consecutive treasures is practically impossible.
Some items may be encountered only once, but this is a rare exception.
The Accountant background increases the probability of filling slots, making the average value of treasures higher.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/3c0d9f08c4de1869efc9742ad0b13501911b6ac3.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/d989652376e8515b50ba848ae6f5d67577f2d659.png[/img]

These are 2 treasures taken right at the start of a new game in free play mode. Note the difference in content with and without the Accountant perk.

[h3]Equipment[/h3]

This category includes melee and firearms, armor, spyglasses, and hats.
It's worth mentioning that in free play mode, quest items from story mode can now be found in treasures.
For example, a katana can be found from tiers 11 to 14.
Each treasure can have 1 to 3 equipment slots filled.

[h3]Valuables[/h3]

This category includes money, jewelry, pearls, gems, crafting items, gold, and doubloons.
At high treasure tiers, you can find extremely valuable items - arrows, bombs, mangarosa, and a few other [b]very special[/b] things.
From 1 to 5 valuable slots can be filled.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/8967479f0db85b95cc8814058e7e996047de5fa5.png[/img]

Here's an example of a high-tier treasure that contained bombs and arrows. Finding it required quite a bit of effort on a character with the Accountant background.

[h3]Special Items[/h3]

This category includes maps, amulets, treasure map fragments, hourglasses, chronometers, and so on.
All amulets are divided by their value to the player at different stages of the game and have a lower tier threshold for appearance, but no upper threshold.
For example, holy water and powder testers can drop at any treasure tier, from 1 to 15.
From 1 to 4 slots can be filled, plus 1 additional slot for a treasure map half, if it can appear.

[h3]Lore Items[/h3]

This section will always contain one item - a note from the treasure. We've prepared numerous small stories, some funny, some sad, which players can collect and keep in a special document in their journal.
Each of these notes appears only once, and players can earn an achievement for collecting all of them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44649887/8dbd2708bae80a0ceb3c1e693d191ae9e5c3e5fa.png[/img]

Here's just one example - someone's story, tragic or comical. Is the author of this note alive? I guess we'll never know.

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]

We hope to make treasure hunting as exciting and unique as possible, as it deserves to be, and we'll emphasize this in a future DLC.
Share your thoughts in [url=https://discord.gg/caribbeanlegend]Discord[/url], and we'll see you in future dev diaries!

[b]Kirill, Black Mark Studio[/b]
:jollyr:

Proofreading of German, Spanish, French and Polish versions, as well as translation into Ukrainian and Hungarian, is already in full swing in the separate Discord translators channel. If you're interested in speeding up the release of official translations, [url=https://discord.gg/WCu6As6DRM]welcome to join us[/url]!

[h2]Mods:[/h2]
We continue to improve support for user modifications.
[list]
[*]Scripts have been moved to [url=https://github.com/nkrapivin/stormworkshoptool/wiki]GitHub[/url]
[*]Added tools for modders to avoid a new game requirement
[*]The engine will have a new function to get a list of mods and their full paths
[*]All documentation in the official [url=https://github.com/nkrapivin/stormworkshoptool/wiki/%D0%A1%D0%BE%D0%B7%D0%B4%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%B5-%D0%BC%D0%BE%D0%B4%D0%BE%D0%B2-%D0%BA-Caribbean-Legend]wiki[/url] will be updated soon
[/list]

[h2]Controls:[/h2]

We've fixed and improved a lot - all thanks to your feedback. But don't limit ourselves with only fixing, we continue to add new features to the new controls and camera scheme. We haven't even begin balancing it though, so the Sharpshooter's background is currently the most overpowered. Seize the moment!

[list]
[*][b]Fixed camera in cutscenes.[/b] There were many complaints about camera glitches in cutscenes. We've made every effort to fix this bug, and now it no longer occurs. If you encounter it again, please let us know

[*][b]Fixed control disabling in combat.[/b] Finding and fixing this problem was difficult, but after significant code rework, the bug no longer appears. If it occurs again, please report it with a detailed description of the conditions

[*][b]Significantly improved maneuverability.[/b] We've reworked the character's reaction speed to button presses, as well as acceleration and deceleration dynamics, especially in combat mode. The mechanism for changing direction during running has been changed — the character no longer performs a long, uncontrollable animation. Now control and positioning are much more convenient

[*][b]Adaptive turning speed.[/b] Many complained about the inconvenience of turning the character with the free camera. Now the turning speed increases depending on the angle of deviation from the camera, allowing quick 180-degree turns almost in place. Finally, people will stop falling in caves

[*][b]Fixed turning in aiming mode.[/b] Character behavior in aiming mode has become significantly smoother and more consistent

[*][b]Improved interaction with NPCs.[/b] Increased responsiveness when interacting with NPCs and improved adaptation to the over-the-shoulder camera

[*][b]Fixed the running issue during looting.[/b] The character no longer continues running in place after activating interaction with objects (searching corpses, chests)

[*][b]Fixed swimming and diving suits.[/b] Underwater swimming and movement in diving suits, including Justice Island, now work correctly

[*][b]Sprint in peaceful mode no longer consumes energy.[/b] You asked — we delivered. There may be minor bugs due to complex interaction with the hostility mode. Report any inconsistencies, and we'll fix them promptly

[*][b]Adaptive camera for swimming.[/b] The long-standing problem with the awkward camera while swimming has been fixed. Now when swimming above water, the camera automatically adjusts, providing an excellent view. We recommend testing it at Justice Island!

[*][b]New strafing animations.[/b] The old sideways running animations looked inappropriate and drew unwanted attention. Now they've been replaced with more realistic and attractive animations

[*][b]Headshots.[/b] Damage from headshots is doubled, combining with critical hits and aiming mechanics. While this mechanic is not yet balanced, enjoy spectacular 1000-damage shots without much effort
[/list]

[h3]To be continued in 1.4[/h3]
